### 2026-11-01: Okay, so this was literally a race against time. I am a procrastinator, so I'll sue myself. I actually started designing on Monday, changed my mind about the simple LED, and tried something else (the

**6.5h**

Okay, so this was literally a race against time. I am a procrastinator, so I'll sue myself. I actually started designing on Monday, changed my mind about the simple LED, and tried something else (the OLED). I sucked at that, so I decided to make a LED matrix, because we love colors in this house.

To design the matrix, I used the guide and tried to personalize it by ending with an image and a few buttons and a rotary encoder switch. The PCB schematics on their own weren't TOO hard to make. I was a bit confused on the connections, though. I was a bit confused on the connection though because I used an XIAO – ESP 32 – C3 – CMD and a lot of connections that I had originally made. As I scrolled down to the Guide, I realized  were wrong.

For example, originally I had made my MTX–DIN label connect to MTDI, which is pin 15, which was wrong, and I had my MTDCLK connected to MTCK, which is 20, which is also wrong, and I had connected my MTX–CS to my D1 pin.

So following the guide, which I should’ve been paying more attention to,  I didn’t connect my labels correctly; therefore, MTD – CLK went to D8, MTXCS to D7, and MTXDIN went to D10, and then I made the appropriate connections on my connector.

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 004450](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/91aa63287f87d05fcaf8e6149abed57dc135e64381f7d4212ad363ba7bd1169f.png)

Then for the additional feature inputs, I actually was not really following the specific logic. I just wanted to vibe, I guess, so I learned a rotary encoder switch is kind of like finding the potential, and it’s the same thing as a slide pot, which is why I chose to put the rotary  encoder instead.

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 004439](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/2f741435feca6f739e98e0d79059c6d78b536468dbb890e96760203cecb0644a.png)

I added a bunch of buttons as well because I wanted to challenge myself. So I didn't use one button, and that made the connections a bit tricky, so I think it took me like two hours to make my schematics.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/fb758aab58ca0ca2d319d48102660d907ce7dda500e468243e608f08bdc9d7d8.png)

Then when I had to edit it, I realized that there was one error, and it was like the main board. The controller wasn’t found, like the footprint wasn't found, so at first I tried to change the footprint in the board, and I was like, "OK, that’s even worse," so I had to actually go into the Seeds Studio GitHub and download the appropriate footprint, so I was figuring it out.

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 001901](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/b4d7ab9fd0b2435e9a6d42e8bfc8c5112c5b3933b491856db07232b6cd7a19db.png)

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 001927](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/61a20346e91a8ee1f4e4490551ffa55151ebc27f4a6af2c70a99d57b0d02227d.png)

### 2026-11-01: # Worked on the GODFORSAKEN README and the firmware code

# Worked on the GODFORSAKEN README and the firmware code

Worked mostly on editing my GitHub. Added images and instructions
Since I learned last week, I also uploaded my work in separate folders: one for the PCB, one for the firmware, and one for the board footprint.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/af74c16cdc534a626eb6c88a6345ca82c0d9252c92c2cd71ba7c7e6f5980fbb6.png)

Also worked on my firmware by editing the base code AND downloading the necessary libraries:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/134d019e049c1e2c52ff87969acea3eef3d584dc7847c72e9cac8f9e045b8016.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/062f48e9ee3d5c815851b105ab10286d9ad03ef9b8f843ec5cc3cc48451ef2e5.png)

Then I was done with it:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/mZKFEMEIAEQ1UpTgazjp9xUySy88SbqC/62a29b43b42eb9bb38bc65cf5ce37700ad96c66f75daf84169c332544f63e20d.png)

I also adjusted pin mappings to match the schematic.
1. BTN_1 on D0
2. BTN_2 on D1
3. BTN_3 on D2
4. ENC_A on D4
5. ENC_B on D5
6. ENC_BTN on D6
7. and CS_PIN on D7

Also added new features because I needed to give the three buttons I added some functionality. I DID ask Gemini for help with the code (newbie at Arduino), like what board to install, how to add these features, and the correct speeds
- Button 1 moves through the text messages.
- Button 2 nchanges the text scroll effect.
- Button 3 changes  display brightness levels.
- Rotary encoder changes the the  scroll speed.
- And the encoder switch resets speed and brightness back to defaults.
